THREE PROVENANCE CLASSES kept distinct. persisted desired RF is a valid replica_count from the authoritative row; BOOTSTRAP EXPECTED RF is that table's schema creation default, usable ONLY to keep initial formation safely blocked while the freshly seeded row becomes observable; authoritative UNKNOWN is missing or invalid policy where evidence is required. The barrier exists to remain BLOCKED, so it may use bootstrap expected RF — and MUST, because a zero target disarms it: a false cohort never latches barrierEngaged and BYPASSED_INSUFFICIENT_COHORT is a RELEASE state, releasing in 50ms in the very window it polices. This exception does NOT extend to authoritative consumers, which report UNKNOWN instead, and a bootstrap default can never turn UNKNOWN into a KNOWN state. Mutation-verified: a literal target, and a zero target, each red this scenario

THE DEFECT THAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, now a permanent negative control. A consumer wrote resolveDesiredReplicationFactor(...).replicationFactor || Number(raw); the decoder returns 0 for every row it REJECTS, so the || arm re-read exactly those inputs with pre-decoder semantics — an inherited value gave 99, an accessor gave 42 AND WAS EXECUTED, "9" gave 9 — while gating voter promotion. This pins that a rejected policy stays rejected at the readiness and promotion decisions, and that no consumer executes an accessor while validating a row. It replaces a camel-alias receipt that was a non-discriminating duplicate of the readiness path
